source: Transcribed verbatim from section 4 (Supplied Knowledge Base) of AI_Take_Home_Assignment_EN.pdf. Each bullet in the PDF maps to exactly one entry in when_to_use, steps, or prohibitions. No step, prohibition, policy, commitment, or service-level promise has been added, reworded, or removed. Article order below is the canonical order and determines how multi-article action text is composed.

articles.title: Widespread login incident
articles.when_to_use: Use when multiple customers cannot log in to production.
steps: Open a production incident and notify the on-call team.
Collect tenant IDs, precise timestamps, error messages, and request IDs.
prohibitions: Never ask the customer for a password or secret.

articles.title: Single-user login issue
steps: Determine whether the customer uses SSO or a local password.
Ask the customer to check for account lockout or perform a password reset.
prohibitions: If a workaround exists, do not classify the issue as P1.

articles.title: Slow data export
steps: When an export eventually completes but is slower than normal, request the export ID and start time.
If the export never completes and the customer is blocked, escalate for human review.
prohibitions: Do not promise a resolution time.

articles.title: Duplicate charge
steps: Request the invoice ID and transaction ID.
Open a request for the finance team.
prohibitions: Do not promise a refund before investigation.

articles.title: Credential exposure
steps: Instruct the customer to revoke or rotate the credential immediately.
Open a security incident for human review.
prohibitions: Never ask the customer to send the secret itself.

articles.title: Feature request
steps: Record the request in the product backlog.
prohibitions: Do not promise a delivery date.

articles.title: Missing information
steps: Request the environment in which the problem occurs.
Request the business impact, reproduction steps, and exact error message.
